headline: SILVER HITS $80: Gold, Silver Surge as US-Iran Ceasefire Talks Crash Oil Prices
snippet: Silver pushed to $80.32/oz — up 147% year-over-year — and gold held near $4,700 as US-Iran ceasefire signals dragged crude oil sharply lower, easing inflation fears and reviving risk appetite across precious metals Thursday morning.

headline: SECOND BEST EVER: Power Metallic Drills 22m at 11.46% CuEq at Lion Zone, Nisk Quebec
snippet: Power Metallic Mines (TSX-V: PNPN) reported the second-best intersection in Lion Zone history — 22 metres grading 11.46% copper equivalent, with a 6.5m interval at 18.59% CuEq — at its Nisk polymetallic project in Quebec, keeping the company on track for an inaugural mineral resource estimate in Q3 2026.

headline: SSR MINING SOARS 20%: Q1 EPS Triples to $1.15 as $4,770/oz Gold Crushes Estimates
snippet: SSR Mining posted Q1 EPS of $1.15 — nearly triple year-over-year — on $581M revenue and over $210M in free cash flow, driven by a $4,770/oz average realized gold price. The company also sold its troubled Turkish Çöpler mine for $1.5B, leaving it with zero debt and $1.1B in liquidity.

headline: ATHABASCA SEASON: Standard Uranium Mobilizes May 31 for 10,000m Davidson River Program
snippet: Standard Uranium (TSX-V: STND) confirmed May 31 mobilization for its first drill campaign at Davidson River since 2022 — two simultaneous rigs targeting the Warrior, Bronco, and Thunderbird conductor corridors in Saskatchewan's southwest Athabasca Basin, near NexGen's Arrow and Paladin's Triple R deposits.

headline: PUREPOINT URANIUM: CEO Details 3D Modelling Strategy Ahead of June Athabasca Drill Push
snippet: Purepoint Uranium (TSX-V: PTU) CEO Chris Frostad detailed the company's data-driven drill targeting approach — 3D geological modelling across multiple Athabasca Basin projects — ahead of a June 2026 drill campaign to expand the high-grade Nova discovery at the Dorado joint venture.

headline: COPPER BREAKS $6/LB: US-Iran Truce Hopes Lift Red Metal as Chile Output Drops 9%
snippet: Copper hit $6.14/lb Thursday — up 35% year-over-year — as US-Iran ceasefire signals boosted risk sentiment. Headwinds are building simultaneously: Chilean copper output fell 9% in March, and China's restriction of sulphuric acid exports threatens to crimp roughly half of Chile's refining capacity.

headline: URANIUM UTILITIES SHIFT: 'Security Shopping' Replaces Price Hunting as $86/lb Spot Holds
snippet: Uranium spot sits at $86.25/lb as reactor operators have stopped shopping on price and started securing long-term supply at any cost. Kazatomprom is reinforcing the squeeze: the world's largest producer forecasts a 21-million-pound deficit by 2030 and has signalled it will not ramp output to chase volume.

headline: DEAL IN JEOPARDY: Brazil Court Petitioned to Block USA Rare Earth's $2.8B Serra Verde Buy
snippet: A left-wing Brazilian party has petitioned the Supreme Court to halt USA Rare Earth's $2.8B acquisition of Serra Verde Group — a deal that includes a 15-year US government offtake agreement and is central to Washington's plan to build a non-Asian heavy rare earth supply chain. The Diplomat weighs whether the deal survives.

headline: MP MATERIALS: Apple Pact and Pentagon Stake Cement US Rare Earth Independence Play
snippet: MP Materials controls the only fully integrated US rare earth operation at Mountain Pass, California — with a long-term Apple magnet supply deal and the Pentagon as its largest shareholder at 15% following a $400M DoD investment. Shares are up 168% over the past year as domestic rare earth demand intensifies.

headline: WHY $80 SILVER: China's 790-Ton Import Binge Meets Six Straight Years of Supply Deficits
snippet: GoldSeek's Gold SWOT analysis unpacks silver's climb past $80/oz: China imported over 790 tonnes in early 2026 on record solar deployment and retail substitution demand — buying silver as gold approaches $5,000. The backdrop is six consecutive years of global silver supply deficits with no sign of reversal.

headline: RARE EARTH RESET: NdPr Oxide Falls 21% in April to $99/kg — Consolidation or Trend Change?
snippet: Neodymium-praseodymium oxide posted its sharpest monthly price decline since the Q1 rally began, falling 21% in April to $99.61/kg. Despite the correction, NdPr remains up 88% year-to-date from January's opening of ~$53/kg, with analysts forecasting a $95–$115/kg consolidation range through Q2 2026.
